newsitem.title: USA: NYS Senate approves school property tax freeze.
newsitem.headline: NYS Senate approves school property tax freeze.

text.p: The New York State Senate approved Wednesday a school property tax freeze and reduction plan that would yield almost $3 billion in tax savings over five years when fully implemented.

The measure "includes direct and indirect property tax relief measures that will add up to almost $3 billion in savings for property taxpayers," said Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, a Republican.
A spokesman for the Senate said the measure will now move to the Democratic-controlled state Assembly.
The spokesman said the measure will become a bargaining issue in the state budget talks. The budget is due by the start of the fiscal year, which is April 1.

The school property tax plan approved by the state Senate would include giving additional state aid to school districts which voluntarily freeze property taxes. School districts could receive three percent of their expenses in additional state aid in return for enacting a tax freeze.
The bill would also establish a statewide school budget voting day on the third Tuesday in May.

And under the measure, schools would have access to pooled financing and construction management services for building projects from the state Dormitory Authority to reduce the cost of capital projects.
